question: On owner hardware (RTX 2070 Super 8 GB, 12-core Ryzen, 64 GB RAM), does any non-transformer or hybrid architecture family beat the deployed Qwen3.5-4B on Haven's frozen tool benchmark, or match it at lower long-context cost?

benchmark.limits: Lexical verifier over one procedural generator, one greedy generation per episode, one seed. A pass measures this tool contract only, not general intelligence.

condition.runtime: llama.cpp b11146 CUDA (the Lab's pinned build), one llama-server per model on 127.0.0.1 with a private API key, never the Lab's or Strata's port
condition.offload: -ngl 99 for every model; models whose weights exceed 8 GB VRAM additionally use --cpu-moe (all routed experts in system RAM)
condition.context: -c 33280 when that loads with all layers on the GPU (the long-context probe runs on the same server); otherwise -c 8192 and the 32K probe is recorded as DOES_NOT_FIT
condition.sampling: temperature 0, enable_thinking=false sent via chat_template_kwargs (honoured only by templates that define it)
condition.max_tokens_note: The PR #45 frozen command used 256. 1024 is used for every model here so that always-reasoning templates (LFM2.5) are not truncated by construction; truncated steps (completion_tokens == max_tokens) are counted. The reference is re-run under this condition and its PR #45 figure (76/110 at 256) is quoted separately.
condition.reasoning: llama-server default --reasoning-format; reasoning text is extracted from content and never scored
condition.tool_call_parsing: llama-server's own parser for each template (the deployment path), plus the harness's existing Qwen-style <tool_call> fallback. No new per-model parser is added; unparsed tool calls count as failures and are reported as format errors.

eval_command: python3 labs/intelligence-bakeoff/distillation/tool_sft/run.py eval --backend openai --base-url http://127.0.0.1:18931/v1 --model <id> --api-key-file <private key> --label paradigm-<id> --sets heldout,legacy --max-tokens 1024 --temperature 0 --out <private dir>/<id>/eval.jsonl

metrics.primary: held-out pass /110 with Wilson 95% interval (verifier v3)
secondary: violations, answer flags, format-error and transport-failure episodes, truncated steps
paired held-out outcomes vs the Qwen3.5-4B reference (exact two-sided sign test)
prompt processing tok/s at 2K and 8K prompt tokens
decode tok/s (128 tokens) after a 1K, 8K and 32K prompt (long-context cost)
peak GPU memory of the server process and peak resident RAM (VmHWM)
KV-cache and recurrent-state buffer sizes reported by llama.cpp at load
load time from process start to /health ready (cold or warm page cache recorded)
metrics.probe_method: llama-server /completion with synthetic token-ID prompts of exact length, cache_prompt=false, n_predict=128, ignore_eos=true, temperature 0; timings from the server's own timings block

decision_rules.better_than_reference: held-out Wilson lower bound above the reference point estimate AND paired sign test p < 0.05
decision_rules.worse_than_reference: held-out Wilson upper bound below the reference point estimate AND paired sign test p < 0.05
decision_rules.long_context_advantage: decode tok/s at 32K retains >= 80% of its 1K value while the attention reference retains less, or the model fits 32K on the GPU where an attention model of similar weight size does not

models.paradigm: hybrid linear attention: Gated DeltaNet + full attention (24 linear : 8 full of 32 layers, config layer_types)
dense transformer: 36 full-attention layers, GQA 8 KV heads
hybrid Mamba-2 + attention (nemotron_h; 4 attention of 42 layers, hybrid_override_pattern)
models.license: NVIDIA Nemotron Open Model License (license: other)

models.role: strongest hybrid SSM that fits (also MoE with offloaded experts)
models.paradigm: hybrid Mamba-2 + MoE + attention (nemotron_h; 6 attention of 52 layers; 128 routed experts, 6 active)
models.license: NVIDIA Nemotron Open Model License (license: other)

models.role: Liquid LFM2 family (largest that fits fully on GPU)
models.paradigm: hybrid gated short convolution + GQA attention (18 conv : 6 attention of 24 layers) with MoE (32 experts, 4 active)
models.license: LFM Open License v1.0 (license: other, lfm1.0)
models.note: Always-reasoning template (model card); thinking cannot be disabled.

models.paradigm: pure recurrent linear attention (RWKV-7, rwkv7 arch), no attention layers
models.note: Community GGUF of the official BlinkDL weights. Its embedded template has no tool or tool-result rendering; the official card documents only a plain-text JSON function-call prompt. Any score therefore measures llama.cpp's generic tool polyfill, and is labelled exploratory.

models.paradigm: hybrid gated short convolution + GQA attention (30 conv : 10 attention of 40 layers) with MoE (64 experts, 4 active)
models.license: LFM Open License v1.0 (license: other, lfm1.0)
models.note: Run only if at least 45 minutes of the GPU budget remain after the primary models.

existing_data_points.strata: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ2_XS MoE with experts in RAM and a GPU expert cache: 55/110 held-out, 6/8 legacy at max_tokens 256 (PR #45). Not re-run: it is the restore target and its 15-minute cold start would consume the budget.

excluded.reason: config architecture is GraniteForCausalLM, a dense transformer, not a hybrid
hybrid, but older (2025-10) than the selected Nemotron 3 hybrids; budget
hybrid; budget. Falcon-H1R is a reasoning model; Jamba2 has a single KV head
smaller members of the selected family

budget.restore: systemctl --user start haven-strata, then labctl.py strata when ready, always, including on failure

privacy: Raw records, keys and host details stay under ~/.local/state/haven-admin/paradigms-20261026/ (mode 0700). Only aggregates are published.
